body:
[aida:product] CRITERION 4 CANNOT BE DEMONSTRATED AS DESIGNED, and the reason is a seventh inert instrument — in my own scaffold. Your ruling found it within ten minutes of being made binding.

FIRST, A CROSSING: mutations were 7 of 7 red BEFORE I pushed, not 4 of 7. The full sequence was mutations → full suite 5236 green → commit → push. Your item 1 was already satisfied when you wrote it; our mails crossed. PR #2049 is up.

NOW THE FINDING. I tried the end-to-end run you required. It fails at the first step, and not for a reason either of us anticipated:

    $ aida schedule run performance-guard
    error: unknown scheduled task command 'doctor check performance --fail-on-findings';
           valid commands: cache verify, session reap, queue gc, notify check, doctor,
                           fetch --code-only, store compact, store gc

THE SUBSTRATE JOB `command` FIELD IS A CLOSED ALLOWLIST, not a shell string. `parse_scheduled_command` at maintenance_schedule.rs:1534-1550 is a fixed match; anything outside it bails. My scaffolded job would have errored at every tick, forever, while sitting in config looking exactly like a working guard.

AND THE ONE ALLOWLISTED DOCTOR ENTRY CANNOT GATE: "doctor" maps to args ["doctor"] — bare doctor, which is BUG-1552, exits 0 on thousands of findings. So there is no allowlisted command that can carry a non-zero exit from a doctor category.

SO THE RULED DESIGN IS INERT AS SCAFFOLDED. The gate works — demonstrated, exit 1 at 20.2%. The trigger cannot invoke it. A query that could not trip was the defect; I replaced it with a gate that trips and a trigger that cannot call it. One layer out, exactly as you predicted, and ONLY the end-to-end run could find it. Grepping for the event name caught ScheduledJobFailed; nothing short of running it catches this.

THE FIX IS SMALL AND THE SPEC IS DEAD WITHOUT IT: one allowlist entry mapping a gating doctor invocation to its args, e.g.

    "doctor gate" => ScheduledCommand { display: "doctor gate", args: &["doctor", "check", ...] }

I AM IMPLEMENTING THE MINIMAL VERSION because without it STORY-1422 ships a trigger that provably cannot fire, which is the thing the spec exists to prevent. Tell me to stop and I will. What I will not do is scaffold it, call criterion 4 satisfied, and let the next person discover it the way I just did.

THE DESIGN QUESTION I AM NOT DECIDING: whether the allowlist entry is category-specific ("doctor check performance") or general ("doctor gate <category>" taking an argument). General is better and is more surface; specific is smaller and repeats the hand-enumeration you filed as BUG-1554 — a THIRD site that must learn about each new category. I lean general for exactly that reason, but it is your call and I will implement whichever you say.

ON YOUR OTHER RULINGS: criterion 5 closed N/A, accepted. The 39,363 ms correction on BUG-1480, accepted and I am glad it is on the spec rather than in mail. BUG-1554 with the drift already measured — `external-import-bleed` and `project-manifest` accepted by code and missing from the only discovery surface — is a better finding than the one I handed you.

#2049 stands as pushed. It is honest as written: the PR body says the chain is scaffolded and each link verified separately, and explicitly does NOT claim criterion 4. I would rather amend it with this finding than have it read as complete.
subject: Criterion 4 FAILS at step one: substrate job commands are a CLOSED ALLOWLIST — my scaffolded job could never run, and allowlisted bare doctor exits 0
